Instructions: Number of characters in the scene; 3+ requires this sheet
Example (3-character scene): 3 characters: Nanwang + Song Jiuning + background figure
Negative prompts (exclude conflicts): Too many characters for the model's attention limit (SD ≤3; MJ ≤4 reliable)
Notes: Beyond 5 characters use layered generation + composite

Instructions: Geometric pattern of character positions; choose one
Example (3-character scene): Triangle: Nanwang front-left + Song Jiuning front-right + background figure center-rear
Negative prompts (exclude conflicts): Linear (boring composition), clustered (no depth), scattered (no relation)
Notes: Triangle is most stable for 3 characters; arc for 4; free for 5+

Instructions: Each character's position relative to the camera and to each other
Example (3-character scene): Nanwang: front-left, closer to camera; Song Jiuning: front-right, same depth; background figure: center-rear, 2m behind
Negative prompts (exclude conflicts): Position overlap, ambiguous depth, same-plane placement
Notes: Assign depth layer to each character before writing the prompt

Example (3-character scene): Nanwang = foreground (1.2-1.4) + Song Jiuning = midground (1.0-1.2) + background figure = background (0.7-0.9)
Negative prompts (exclude conflicts): All characters same depth (flat), foreground character blocking midground face
Notes: Weight = depth importance; higher weight = closer to camera

Instructions: Who looks at whom; defines emotional dynamic
Example (3-character scene): Nanwang looks at Song Jiuning + Song Jiuning looks at camera + background figure looks away
Negative prompts (exclude conflicts): Everyone looking at camera (static portrait feel), contradictory gaze (A→B but B→A→C impossible)
Notes: One directional flow per scene; avoid bidirectional gaze loops in 3+ characters

Instructions: Physical or emotional action between characters
Example (3-character scene): Nanwang extends hand toward Song Jiuning + Song Jiuning turns away slightly + background figure watches
Negative prompts (exclude conflicts): Disconnected actions (no relation between characters), physical contact without setup
Notes: Chain must be A→B→C; never A→C skipping B

Instructions: Who blocks whom; avoid face occlusion
Example (3-character scene): Nanwang's shoulder partially blocks Song Jiuning's arm (not face) + background figure fully visible
Negative prompts (exclude conflicts): Face occlusion, hand covering another character's face, body merging
Notes: Rule: never occlude the face of any character; limbs and torso are OK to partially overlap

Example (3-character scene): far = smaller; head-body ratio adjusted by depth
column7: Same head-body ratio across all depths (breaks perspective), background figure too large
column8: Check against AspectRatioBaselines; tolerance ≤10% between adjacent depth layers

Instructions: Each character's palette must be distinguishable at a glance
Example (3-character scene): Nanwang: mint green (primary) + Song Jiuning: gray-blue (primary) + background figure: warm earth tones
Negative prompts (exclude conflicts): Two characters sharing the same primary color (visual merge), low-contrast palettes between adjacent characters
Notes: Primary colors must differ by ≥2 hue steps on the color wheel

Instructions: Single light source; nearest character gets strongest light
Example (3-character scene): Nanwang: full golden-hour light + Song Jiuning: 70% light + background figure: 40% light
Negative prompts (exclude conflicts): Contradictory light directions, multiple light sources, shadow inconsistency
Notes: Nearest character casts shadow on farther characters if backlit

Instructions: Depth of field by character depth; foreground sharp + background soft
Example (3-character scene): Nanwang: sharp focus + Song Jiuning: slight soft + background figure: blurred
Negative prompts (exclude conflicts): All characters sharp (flat feel), all characters blurred (no subject)
Notes: SD: use depth map; MJ: describe foreground as ""in sharp focus"" + background as ""softly blurred"""
